title: Which outcome changes the estimate?
hook: Compare an outcome with the prediction it replaces.

knows: The listed prerequisite concepts and small arithmetic.
doesNotKnow: Distinguish TD prediction error from reward size.

misconception: Distinguish TD prediction error from reward size.
objective: Distinguish TD prediction error from reward size.

claims.text:
All finite inputs, equations, computed outputs and visual encodings: export function update(old:number,reward:number,next:number,terminal=false){const target=reward+(terminal?0:.5*next),delta=target-old;return {old,reward,next,terminal,target,delta,value:old+.5*delta};}
export function run(mode:number){return [()=>update(4,2,4),()=>update(4,4,4),()=>update(10,10,99,true),()=>update(4,0,99,true)][mode]();}

Which produces a larger upward correction: current 4, reward 4, next 4; or current 10, terminal reward 10?; options ['Reward 4 case', 'Reward 10 case', 'Equal correction']; correct index 0
claims.source: https://jmvidal.cse.sc.edu/library/sutton88a.pdf (TD update context; acquisition separately recorded). Exact fixture derived locally in model.ts and exercised by model.repro.mjs; source context does not verify local numbers.

claims.text: The retained reward 4 produced target 6 against old value 4, so error 2 raised the estimate to 5. Terminal reward 10 matched its old prediction 10: error zero, no correction. Reward size alone did not determine the update. A negative target-minus-old gap decreases the estimate even when the reward is nonnegative.
